correctness.rationale: For any finite side-preserving group G transitive on nonempty X,Y, a fixed realization point has invariant support and constant barycentric weights on edge orbits. Every G-orbit of bipartite edges projects surjectively onto X and Y; if an orbit is a matching, these projections are injective, forcing equal shore cardinality and a G-equivariant bijection f:X→Y with graph in E. Conversely graph(f) is one orbit by transitivity; any two admissible orbits cannot coexist in a matching because each uses every shore vertex. Thus invariant supports consist of exactly one admissible orbit and its single barycenter, proving the PL-discrete classification and Z^(N−1) reduced H0. For K_n,n identical actions the supported bijections form C_Sn(G), whose order≤n because a commuting permutation fixing one label fixes all; regular groups attain n, 2-transitive degree>2 has centralizer order1. Checked 28 independently generated small invariant shore-transitive bipartite graph cases against actual invariant matchings. No finite check is extrapolated to all groups.

value.rationale: This classifies actual geometric fixed spaces of the entire natural family of shore-transitive bipartite matching complexes, including empty cases, complete boards and full residual integral H0. It separates geometric fixed sets (possibly multiple barycenters) from falsely using the fixed-vertex subcomplex, a useful structural equivariant-topology distinction; extends a centralizer count to arbitrary invariant bipartite subgraphs.
